title: Path Sum
statement_short: Given the root of a binary tree and an integer targetSum, return true if the tree has a root-to-leaf path such that adding up all the values along the path equals targetSum. A leaf is a node with no children.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in tree <= 5000, -1000 <= Node.val <= 1000, -1000 <= targetSum <= 1000
hint: Node count up to 5000 allows recursive path sum subtraction from root to leaf in O(n) time.
keywords: adding up all the values along the path equals targetSum
why_not: Right: Tree DFS subtracts current node value from targetSum down to leaf nodes in O(n) time and O(h) space. Not Tree BFS: Level-order queue traversal tracking running node sums also works in O(n) time, but uses extra queue space. Not Prefix Sum: Prefix sums evaluate arbitrary subsegment sums, whereas path sum evaluates whole root-to-leaf paths. Not Backtracking: Backtracking collects all matching paths, whereas checking existence requires a simple boolean recursive check.
